label: Root links from Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae
summary: I q.10 a.1 ad 2: illud quod est vere aeternum, non solum est ens, sed vivens: Aquinas accepts the Boethian definition and insists that what is truly eternal lives. Applying it to the case predicate requires both directions of calibration, including how perfect possession is represented by life with no beginning, end or succession in the supplied frame. I q.10 a.1 co.: Sic ergo ex duobus notificatur aeternitas: The passage specifies absence of beginning and end and of succession. The case still needs the living witness and an interpretation of the three frame predicates sufficient for perfect possession of life, with both directions of the proposed calibration. I q.10 a.4 co.: dato quod tempus semper fuerit et semper futurum sit: Aquinas gives a reason to deny that endless time captures proper eternity: succession remains even if time has no start or finish. To witness failure of the case calibration one still needs a being in the supplied profile that has the relevant endless-life conditions and fails primitive Eternal, or the converse mismatch. I q.10 a.5 co., ad 2 and ad 3: aevum est totum simul: The aevum example specifies why all-at-once in an underlying duration is insufficient when change can accompany it. The case needs its NoLifeSuccession predicate to test the relevant succession of the whole life, and the remaining life, boundary and perfect-possession conditions must calibrate primitive Eternal. I q.19 a.1 ad 2: Aquinas explicitly includes loving and delighting in possessed good within the will. Applying the claim requires identifying the resting in the target with that kind of enjoyment of an intellectually apprehended good, and separately accounting for the seeking disjunct. I q.19 a.2 co.: Aquinas takes willing to permit communication of an already possessed good and applies it to divine will. The case needs more than compatibility: giving the recipient esse must itself be willing that same recipient's actual GOOD_4, with the same giver and recipient. I q.2 a.3 co., quinta via: Ergo est aliquid intelligens, a quo omnes res naturales ordinantur ad finem: The Fifth Way concludes that one intelligent being orders all natural things to an end. The case needs natural bodies and their end-direction to instantiate the stated scope and relation, and the directing witness itself to be a first mover moved by none. I q.2 a.3 co., tertia via: quod omnes dicunt Deum: The Third Way calls what is necessary through itself and causes necessity in others God. Applying the conclusion to the case requires its first NECESSARY_1 bearer to be this same cause, and the relevant source of necessity to count as first cause in the GOD_2 naming sense. I q.2 a.3 obj. 1: Si ergo Deus esset, nullum malum inveniretur: Objection 1 argues from infinite goodness to the absence of any evil. The Rowe-frame challenge concerns a more specific permission constraint. The earlier objection tests a stricter interpretation, requiring an independent link between goodness and nonpermission that addresses Aquinas’s reply about goods from permitted evils. I q.3 a.5 co., first proof: species constituitur ex genere et differentia; id a quo sumitur differentia ... sicut actus ad potentiam: The source's first reason treats genus and constituting difference as taken from what stands as potency and act. The application needs every proper genus inclusion in the case to work that way and the same GOD_4 witness to lack the relevant potency. I q.3 a.5 co., third proof: omnia quae sunt in genere uno ... differant in eis esse et quod quid est: The source argues that the members of a genus share generic quiddity but differ in their acts of being. The application needs the resulting esse–essence distinction for every proper generic member and identity of represented esse and essence for the same GOD_4 witness. I q.80 a.1 ad 2: Aquinas distinguishes grasping an object as being from the suitably good aspect under which appetite bears on it. This bears on the target's good-as-apprehended reading. It leaves open that this same divine intellectual act apprehends a good through a form and that the form actualizes in the selected sense. I q.9 a.2 co.: mutabile potest aliquid dici dupliciter: Aquinas attributes the continued esse of creatures to the creator's current action, distinguishing power in another from intrinsic mutability. To use it here, the contingent bearers at w must all fall under its creature scope and the continuing giver must instantiate the distinct actual CAUSE_2 relation at that same w. I-II q.94 a.2 co.: praecepta legis naturae hoc modo se habent ad rationem practicam, sicut principia prima demonstrationum se habent ad rationem speculativam: utraque enim sunt quaedam principia per se nota: The passage places primary precepts in practical reason and its ensuing explanation grounds the first in the good. Application requires matching the source's pursuit and avoidance imperatives and practically apprehended good to the target's selected vocabulary.
